reasoning: Hard gates fail: kelvin_ok=false with 3 Kelvin net instances unrouted (SENSEC1_HI and SENSEC1_LO from cable 1; SENSEC2_HI from cable 2), structural DRC=43, and 7 unconnected ratlines. The directed stub summary is a textbook compiler_kelvin_omission: n_stubs=7 but the compiler's nets list contains only [/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA] — zero Kelvin nets — and all 7 stubs were fully eliminated before FR (absorbed=3, trimmed_spurs=2, removed_orphans=2 = n_stubs exactly). Rules 33/34/35 should have been firing for multiple consecutive rounds. The novel finding for this round is an ASYMMETRIC Kelvin pair state on cable 2: /SENSEC2_HI appears in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines, but /SENSEC2_LO does NOT — meaning cable 2's LO member is apparently routed while its HI member is not. This is distinct from cable 1's total-pair failure. The metric kelvin_unrouted=1 counts only fully-unrouted pairs (cable 1, both members unconnected) and therefore does not signal the cable-2 partial failure; that failure is only represented in the unconnected count. The practical consequence is that FR's existing route for /SENSEC2_LO occupies escape geometry at the shunt inner edge and physically blocks /SENSEC2_HI — force-injecting a stub for SENSEC2_HI alone cannot resolve this because FR treats the routed LO member as fixed copper. None of the 50 standing rules address this asymmetric-pair case or the rip-up-both corrective action it requires. Scorer penalties are already comprehensive for the observed metrics (kelvin_unrouted at 1000, gate_fail at 1000, unconnected at 450); raising any weight further would not resolve a compiler omission or an asymmetric-route blockage at the shunt. The new manager rule closes the asymmetric-pair gap.
manager_rule: When failing_reasons for round R shows that for any cable index N, exactly ONE member of the Kelvin pair (/SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO) has 'has unconnected ratlines' while the other member does NOT appear in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines — an asymmetric-unrouted state where one member is routed but the other is not — AND this same asymmetric condition for cable N was also present in failing_reasons for the immediately preceding round R-1: (1) before FR dispatch for round R+1, issue an explicit rip-up directive for BOTH /SENSEC{N}_HI AND /SENSEC{N}_LO, removing the existing route of the 'good' member so FR re-routes the pair from scratch without being constrained by the blocking prior path; (2) inject a symmetric Kelvin stub pair for cable N with mandatory_kelvin_bypass flag active (per Rule 34), bypassing the compiler priority gate, absorber merge/trim, and orphan-removal stages entirely; (3) log 'kelvin_asymmetric_ripup' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index N, (c) the member that was unrouted (failing), (d) the member ripped up despite being routed, (e) any bounding-box occupancy data from a Rule 35/36 congestion query if one was executed this round. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 35, and 36 and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate. Rationale: after 2+ consecutive rounds in the asymmetric state, the routed member demonstrably occupies geometry that prevents the unrouted member from escaping the shunt inner edge; stub injection for the failing member alone cannot succeed because FR treats the routed member's copper as fixed; only ripping both and re-routing as a symmetric pair from the same shunt restores the geometric freedom needed to satisfy the Kelvin gate.
